title: Conflict Protocol
concept: Takes a fight from ‘are we calm enough?’ to ‘who does what next’, so it ends in a change, not a stand-off.
whenToUse: When a fight has started, or it’s the one you keep having, and you can both still be kind to each other, or a Pause + Return has brought you back to calm.
steps: Check if you’re calm — if either of you is flooded, take a Pause + Return first.
Warm up — say one warm, true thing.
Make it safe — remind each other you’re not breaking up.
Say what happened — one of you puts it this way: “When X happened, I felt Y; here’s the impact.”
Ask for one thing — be specific.
Listen in the right order — first hear how it landed, then what would help, and only then their side.
Get proof if you need it — if something needs to change, turn it into a Proof item (Proof Protocol card).
Line up next steps — agree who does what, and when you’ll check back.

phrases.text: I’m on your team, even though I’m frustrated.
Can we soften the room first?
I think we’re in Reach–Recoil. Twenty-minute pause?

working: B opens: “I’m on your team, even though I’m frustrated.” A hears how the missed pickup hit B before explaining. They agree one ask and put a check-in in the diary, then eat dinner together.
notWorking: A opens with “Why didn’t you text about the pickup?” and nothing kind first. A cross-examines, B goes quiet, and by nine they’re both arguing about the tone, not the pickup.
activity: Practise once on a minor gripe, with a timer. The one listening keeps you both to the order, gently.
